scorecard.rationale: One four-arm randomized adolescent conference abstract reports lower anxiety in the banana-only arm (regression -7.84, p<.001; preparation and full methods unavailable), alongside a nonrandom inpatient Ambon-banana comparison with baseline imbalance and a postoperative trial with conflicting reported t statistics (PMID40331125). Competing evidence includes a small null randomized healthy-adult Cavendish banana trial (n=20), uncontrolled Parkinson individualized nutrition with banana-flavored liquid, and separate levodopa-interaction observations without anxiety scores. No controlled Parkinson raw-banana anxiety trial exists; the adolescent randomized abstract sustains only a minimal_signal against worsening. The mental health review names banana among dietary prebiotics without comparing raw banana with another exposure on an anxiety measure. It supplies no independent direction. The fruit review includes banana in a fruit antioxidant comparison and does not measure anxiety attributable to eating raw banana. Prior clinical contrasts remain the basis of the weak inverse sign. The Lee original reports higher plasma salsolinol after banana in healthy adults, with no clear corresponding change in sampled rat brain regions under a separate experiment. Neither branch measures anxiety or clinical Parkinson efficacy.
